clue.text: Take a quick look at first of cases in hospital

indicators.note: the picked letter is put inside the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents

indicators.note: the opening letter alone of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor glances over the first patient admitted to a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page is to read it rapidly, running the eye over it without close study.

clue.text: Conservative lot leading their opponents in desire for manufacturers?

indicators.note: leading means placed in front of what follows

parts.note: a heap is a lot, a large amount
Labour is the party opposing the Conservatives

explanation.surface: Tories ahead of their rivals in what industrialists want.
explanation.walkthrough: The opponents of the Conservatives are Labour; the question mark marks the definition as a wry description.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory owners wanting low costs would welcome workers paid little, so cheap labour is what they crave.

clue.text: Equipment for tennis professional with suitable final income

parts.note: a net is strung across a tennis court
pro is short for professional
fit means suitable, appropriate

explanation.surface: A tennis pro buys kit, hoping for good earnings in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is what remains of revenue after all costs are deducted, the bottom-line earnings.

clue.text: Bet meat and oil are processed as essential for life

indicators.note: food that is processed is broken down and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dietary claim that a mix of beef and oil keeps the body going.
explanation.definitionFit: A metabolite is a substance made or used in metabolism, the chemistry that keeps an organism alive.

clue.text: What's hot sun cracking wet earth?

indicators.note: breaking into something, so the star is placed within the mud

parts.note: mud is wet earth
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: Sun beating down cracks wet ground, a riddle about heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent condiment whose sharp taste is described as hot or fiery.

clue.text: A tortuous clue somehow about the Spanish painter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the Spanish article
somehow suggests things arranged in some unspecified way, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: EL is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A setter admits a twisted clue about a Spanish painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal rearranges A TORTUOUS CLUE to TOULOUSAUTREC, and 'about' puts that around EL. The 'Spanish painter' is a false trail: he was French.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French artist famous for his Montmartre posters and paintings.

clue.text: I'm less than impressed with mammoth trade

parts.note: mammoth means huge, big
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A shrug at news of an enormous commercial agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sarcastic retort meaning 'so what?', dismissing something as unimportant.

clue.text: Home gets consent to opening

parts.note: being in means being at home
to let is to allow, consent to

explanation.surface: A homeowner gets permission to open up.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea or a gap through which something enters.

clue.text: Bible books exist to be raised as a source of inspiration

indicators.note: in a down entry raising something reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of Bible books
are means exist, as in 'there are'

explanation.surface: Holy scripture held up as a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the patroness of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Good painter works hard over place with famous address

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter of nudes

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense of turning over, the word is read backwards

parts.note: to grub is to dig or toil laboriously, so grubs means works hard

explanation.surface: A fine artist toils over a location known for a famous speech.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUBS read backwards gives SBURG. The famous address is Lincoln's Gettysburg Address of 1863.
explanation.definitionFit: Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, is the site where Abraham Lincoln delivered his celebrated speech after the Civil War battle.

clue.text: Appeal of the Parisian father's embraced

indicators.note: the French article is held inside the word for father, as in a hug

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father; the 's stands for has
LE is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A French father hugged by his child, with an appeal in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or entreaty, which is what an appeal is.

clue.text: Militaristic state's ability in spring

indicators.note: the word for ability goes inside the word for spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
art means skill or ability, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A warlike nation's talent shows up in the springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Sparta was a Greek city-state organised around military training and warfare.

clue.text: A few high on old tower

indicators.note: someone high on drugs is out of their usual state, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A handful of people get high on an old tower.
explanation.definitionFit: One or two is an idiom for a small number, a couple or so.

clue.text: Circle pub argument — something to be carried on outside?

definitions.text: something to be carried on outside?

parts.note: a wheel is a circle
a bar is a pub
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A pub argument spills into the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener uses this one-wheeled cart outdoors to carry loads such as soil.

clue.text: Mistake demolishing English house?

indicators.note: demolishing knocks something down, so the letter for English is removed

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A blunder that ends with an English house being knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaff is British slang for a home, as in 'come round to my gaff'; the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a gaff is someone's home or flat, the place where they live.

clue.text: Not happy in place surrounded by sick

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place sits inside the word for sick

parts.note: diseased means sick, ill
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy at being stuck among the ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeased means annoyed or dissatisfied, the opposite of content.

clue.text: Weary time in plant garden with elders

indicators.note: the letters for weary and time go inside the plant

parts.note: the arum is a plant, such as the arum lily
to bore someone is to weary them

explanation.surface: Bored with the time spent in a garden among older folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Elders here are elder trees, not older people.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden of trees, which might include elder trees.

clue.text: Personal qualities frequently destroy repeatedly on board?

indicators.note: being on board means inside a ship, so these letters go within the ship's letters

parts.note: the letter S repeated gives SS, the steamship that 'on board' calls for
oft is an old word for often, frequently
kills is the verb for destroying, here in the form the answer needs

explanation.surface: Personal traits that keep wrecking things on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the convention of putting letters inside SS, a steamship; the setter means both OFT and KILL to sit in SS, sharing the middle S.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft skills are interpersonal abilities such as communication and teamwork, as distinct from technical expertise.

clue.text: His rank is unusual for a deity

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A god whose status is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a major Hindu god, an avatar of Vishnu.

clue.text: Outfit without basis to work on a newspaper?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the suit goes around the basis

parts.note: a suit is an outfit of clothes
a bed is a foundation or base, as in bedrock

explanation.surface: Someone without a solid basis heading off to work on a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor checks and corrects copy for a paper, so to subedit is to prepare articles for print.

clue.text: Holiday island where I party after going back

indicators.note: I comes after the reversed party in the answer
going back means the party's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A tourist describes an island where they partied before heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island famous as a tourist and holiday destination.

clue.text: Support for prayer was intrusive and regularly mixed up

parts.note: pried means poked one's nose in, was intrusive

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one from these words

explanation.surface: A nosy person who got their prayers muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed up' looks like an anagram signal, but 'regularly' takes its even letters, I, E, U.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk with a ledge for a book, used during devotions.

clue.text: Each year having a written test

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: An annual written examination.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is often called a paper, the sheet of questions sat in one session.

clue.text: Island place

parts.note: to lay something is to place it down

explanation.walkthrough: Islay is a Hebridean island off western Scotland known for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides, a place famous for its distilleries.

clue.text: Drunken Arabs caught producing wine

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Tipsy Arabs are caught making wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Light pressure used with beer

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A pale ale poured under gas pressure in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale describes a light colour, one with little depth of hue.

clue.text: Present daily record outside parliament, ultimately like many peers

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: the record wraps around the picked letter

parts.note: a diary records each day's events

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A daily journal kept by someone present in parliament describes the lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers are members of the British House of Lords, many of whom once sat by right of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Many peerages pass down a family by inheritance, so those lords hold titles by birth.

clue.text: Train around area for annual race meeting

indicators.note: the train's name goes around the letter for area

parts.note: the Royal Scot is a famous express train from London to Glasgow

explanation.surface: Taking the train around the area to a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is the June horse-racing meeting at Ascot in Berkshire, attended by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a five-day horse-racing event held every summer at Ascot racecourse.

clue.text: Cut record company putting out books

indicators.note: putting out means removing, so the Bible books leave the label's name

parts.note: Motown is the Detroit record label
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A record label cuts back, putting out books instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting out' suggests a label releasing records, but here it means ejecting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown is the past participle of mow, said of grass that has been cut.
